case_text:
Vignette:
An 18-year-old man presents with dry, cracked lips that have persisted for the past 2 weeks. He reports the condition worsened with the onset of cold, dry winter weather. He admits to habitual lip-licking throughout the day. He denies any angular fissures, oral lesions, recent new lip products, or medications such as isotretinoin. He has no history of atopic dermatitis. On examination, the vermilion border of both lips is dry with fine vertical fissures and mild peeling. There is no bleeding, crusting, or angular cheilitis. The perioral skin is mildly dry but not erythematous. The oral mucosa is normal.
